RE: Formal Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Reference Number: POC-A5F6D22435-38075
Member: Rowan Brooks (ID W772624569)
Date of Notice: 2026-08-07
Denied Service: Total hip replacement, CPT 27130
Appeal Deadline Stated in Notice: 2027-02-03

To Whom It May Concern:

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for a total hip replacement (CPT 27130), as set out in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-07 (Reference POC-A5F6D22435-38075). This appeal is being submitted well within the 180-day deadline stated in that notice.

1. Stated Reason for Denial

The notice gives the following reason for denial: "the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure." I ask that this determination be reversed, or in the alternative that the specific written criteria applied to reach it be produced so that this appeal can be supplemented, for the reasons below.

2. The Governing Clinical Criteria

Security Health Plan's own provider materials state that authorization for joint-surgery procedures, including hip replacement, is administered through eviCore, and eviCore's clinical-guideline lookup tool shows no Security Health Plan-specific modification of its standard guideline for this service. The applicable eviCore guideline document is titled "CMM-313: Hip Replacement/Arthroplasty," part of eviCore's Comprehensive Musculoskeletal Management Guidelines.

I was able to obtain and am quoting only the following language directly from that document (version 2.0.2025, effective November 5, 2025):

- On the standard for review: "The determination of medical necessity for the performance of hip resurfacing and hip replacement (partial or total) is always made on a case-by-case basis."
- On comorbidities: "For individuals with significant medical conditions or comorbidities, the risk/benefit of hip arthroplasty procedures should be clearly documented in the medical record."
- Defining the procedure at issue: "Total Hip Replacement[:] a surgical technique that involves the removal of the damaged hip joint which is then replaced with an artificial prosthesis composed of two or three different components: 1) the head that replaces the original femoral head; 2) the femoral component (a metal stem placed into the femur); and, 3) the acetabular component that is implanted into the acetabulum. The stem may be secured using bone cement or press-fit for the bone to grow into it."
- The document's own radiographic osteoarthritis grading scale (Tönnis Classification System), which it uses to describe imaging severity: "Grade 1: sclerosis of the joint with slight joint space narrowing and osteophyte formation, and no or slight loss of femoral head sphericity[;] Grade 2: small cysts in the femoral head or acetabulum with moderate joint space narrowing and moderate loss of femoral head sphericity[;] Grade 3: large cysts in the femoral head or acetabulum, severe joint space narrowing or obliteration of the joint space, and severe deformity and loss of femoral head sphericity."

I want to be transparent that, despite repeated attempts to obtain the complete document, I was not able to retrieve the specific bulleted "Total Hip Replacement Indications" section of CMM-313 (the section that would state the exact imaging/clinical thresholds for non-resurfacing total hip replacement itself, i.e., CPT 27130). I am not quoting or paraphrasing that section because I have not seen its actual text, and I am not attributing any specific indication list to the plan beyond what is quoted above. I am formally requesting, under the plan's claims-procedure obligations, that Security Health Plan and/or eviCore provide the complete, specific internal rule or criterion actually relied upon to deny this request, so that I and Dr. Lindqvist may respond to it point by point if any deficiency remains.

I would note, without asserting that it is the controlling section for CPT 27130, that the same CMM-313 document's parallel section for total hip resurfacing arthroplasty (a related but distinct procedure) reads: "Total hip resurfacing arthroplasty is considered medically necessary when ALL of the following criteria have been met: … Imaging shows EITHER of the following findings: Osteoarthritis or an inflammatory arthritis affecting BOTH the femoral head and the acetabulum, with joint space narrowing on weight-bearing radiographs … Symptoms include BOTH of the following: Function-limiting pain at short distances (e.g., walking less than ¼ mile, limiting activity to two city blocks, the equivalent to walking the length of a shopping mall) for at least three (3) months duration … Loss of hip function which interferes with the ability to carry out age-appropriate activities of daily living and/or demands of employment … Failure of provider-directed non-surgical management for at least three (3) months duration." I raise this only to show that the same guideline family, when addressing hip arthroplasty for osteoarthritis, relies on the same categories of evidence documented in my record below — weight-bearing imaging findings, duration and severity of function-limiting pain, and duration of failed conservative treatment.

3. Clinical Evidence Supporting Medical Necessity

Applying the case-by-case standard and the categories of evidence identified above to my own record:

- Duration and severity of symptoms: I have had 24 months of progressive hip pain that is not relieved by rest.
- Imaging: A weight-bearing AP pelvis radiograph on 2026-06-09 showed joint space narrowed to 1 mm superolaterally with subchondral sclerosis and osteophytes — the same radiographic features (joint space narrowing, sclerosis, osteophyte formation) the plan's own Tönnis Classification System quoted above uses to grade hip osteoarthritis. [Dr. Lindqvist's office should confirm the specific Tönnis/Kellgren-Lawrence grade assigned to this film, as the imaging report excerpted for this appeal does not itself state a numeric grade.]
- Exam findings: Positive provocative testing on the affected side and range of motion limited by pain.
- Functional impairment: I ambulate with a cane, am limited to walking one block, and cannot put on my own shoes without assistance — a level of disability that, on its face, exceeds the "function-limiting pain at short distances" and "loss of hip function which interferes with the ability to carry out age-appropriate activities of daily living" standard quoted above from the plan's own guideline.
- Failed conservative care exceeding three months in every modality:
  - Physical therapy: 16 weeks (2026-02-22 to 2026-06-14), 16 visits completed, focused on hip abductor strengthening and gait, per the physical therapy discharge note.
  - Medication: NSAIDs for 6 months with inadequate relief.
  - Injection: Corticosteroid injection on 2026-03-29 giving only 3 weeks of partial relief.
- No contraindications: No active infection, no untreated substance use, BMI 29, non-smoker — factors relevant to the guideline's instruction, quoted above, that "the risk/benefit of hip arthroplasty procedures should be clearly documented in the medical record" for individuals with comorbidities; here there are no significant comorbidities that would weigh against surgery.
- Surgeon: This procedure has been recommended by Dr. Lindqvist, MD, orthopedic surgery. [Attach Dr. Lindqvist's supporting letter of medical necessity, NPI, and contact information.]

4. Requested Action

I respectfully request that Security Health Plan:

1. Reverse the denial and approve prior authorization for total hip replacement (CPT 27130); or
2. If the denial is not fully reversed on this record, provide in writing the complete, specific criterion or guideline section actually applied to this request (including the exact "Total Hip Replacement Indications" language from CMM-313, or any other document actually used), so that I may supplement this appeal within the remaining appeal period; and
3. Confirm receipt of this appeal in writing, along with the applicable internal-appeal decision timeframe and my further appeal rights, including the right to an independent external review through the Wisconsin Office of the Commissioner of Insurance if this internal appeal is unsuccessful.

Enclosures:
- Physical therapy discharge note (2026-02-22 to 2026-06-14, 16 visits)
- Medication/treatment history (NSAID trial; corticosteroid injection dated 2026-03-29)
- Weight-bearing AP pelvis radiograph and report, dated 2026-06-09
- Clinic exam notes documenting provocative testing and range-of-motion findings
- Letter of medical necessity from Dr. Lindqvist, MD [to be attached]
- Copy of the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-07

Please direct all correspondence regarding this appeal to me at the address and phone number above, with a copy to Dr. Lindqvist's office at [provider office address/fax].

Sincerely,

Rowan Brooks
Member ID: W772624569

cc: Lindqvist, MD, Orthopedic Surgery [office address/fax]
